why: Self-management means taking an active role in recovery. It does not mean handling every problem alone or avoiding appropriate care.

slides.title: Use What You Know
slides.content: Apply the tools you have practised: understand the context, choose a manageable action, review the response, and adjust when needed.

slides.title: Solve the Next Problem
slides.content: Recovery plans need to change when goals, symptoms, health, work, stress, or life circumstances change. Problem-solving is part of the skill.

slides.title: Keep Partnership Available
slides.content: Professional support may be useful for new or concerning symptoms, stalled progress, uncertainty, significant distress, or decisions that need clinical guidance.

slides.title: Support Capability
slides.content: The purpose of care is not dependence or abandonment. Useful support helps you understand, decide, practise, and return to meaningful activity.

slides.title: Teach It Back
slides.content: Complete this sentence: I can usually manage ___ by ___. I will seek support when ___.
